name: Microsoft Sentinel: pull incidents
description: Every 5 minutes, lists Microsoft Sentinel incidents created since the previous run in one workspace (Azure Resource Manager, app-only OAuth2) and creates one pending alert per incident (source ms-sentinel, deduplicated on the incident name/GUID).

params.help: Subscription that holds the Sentinel workspace.

params.help: Resource group of the Log Analytics workspace.

params.help: Name of the Log Analytics workspace Sentinel is enabled on.

setup:
## Azure side
1. Entra ID > App registrations > New registration (single tenant). Create a client secret.
2. On the Sentinel workspace (or its resource group): Access control (IAM) > Add role assignment > **Microsoft Sentinel Reader** > the app's service principal. No API permission or admin consent is needed: Azure Resource Manager authorises by RBAC role.
3. Store the app id and secret as `SENTINEL_CLIENT_ID` and `SENTINEL_CLIENT_SECRET`, each allowed for `login.microsoftonline.com` and `management.azure.com` (the token host and the API host).

## How it works
- Token: `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token`, client credentials, scope `https://management.azure.com/.default`.
- `GET https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/<ws>/providers/Microsoft.SecurityInsights/incidents?api-version=2025-09-01&$filter=properties/createdTimeUtc ge <since>&$orderby=properties/createdTimeUtc asc&$top=100`.
- One alert per incident: external id = incident `name` (GUID), title = `#<incidentNumber> <title>`, severity High high, Medium medium, Low low, Informational info. Payload = the incident resource (includes `incidentUrl`).
- Incidents are pulled on creation only; later status or severity changes in Sentinel are not synced. Re-reading an incident returns the existing alert.

## Limits
- ponytail: one page per run: at most **100 incidents per window**, oldest first; `nextLink` is not followed.
- A non-200 answer fails the run with `Sentinel incidents pull failed: HTTP <status>`; 403 usually means the role assignment is missing or still propagating.

Docs: [Incidents - List](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/securityinsights/incidents/list?view=rest-securityinsights-2025-09-01), [Client credentials flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-client-creds-grant-flow), [Sentinel roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/roles).
